m.chalisa.do1: Victory to Brahmā, victory to the Self-born, the four-faced one, root of happiness. Show grace to your own servant and remain ever favourable.
m.chalisa.do2: You are the creator of the universe; Aja, Vidhi and Dhātā are your names. Creator of the world, show your lovely grace to your devotee.
m.chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory to the lotus-seated one, root of the world. Remain ever favourable to your devotees.
m.chalisa.cau2: Your four-armed form is supremely lovely; you have faces turned to all four directions.
m.chalisa.cau3: Your handsome body is red in colour; on your head is an imposing mass of matted locks.
m.chalisa.cau4: Above it shines a crown; your white beard shines with great splendour.
m.chalisa.cau5: Wearing white garments you look handsome; your sacred thread is most charming.
m.chalisa.cau6: Lovely earrings shine in your ears; a garland of pearls graces your neck.
m.chalisa.cau7: It was you who revealed all four Vedas and taught divine knowledge to the three worlds.
m.chalisa.cau8: Brahmaloka is your auspicious abode; your fame has spread through all the worlds.
m.chalisa.cau9: Your consort is Sāvitrī, whose other name, dwelling in the heart, is Gāyatrī.
m.chalisa.cau10: Lovely Sarasvatī is your daughter, player of the vīṇā, beautiful in every way.
m.chalisa.cau11: You remain seated on your lotus seat; you have arrayed every adornment of devotion to Hari.
m.chalisa.cau12: The lord of the gods, Viṣṇu, lay asleep on the ocean of milk; from his navel an incomparable lotus appeared.
m.chalisa.cau13: On it you are seated, merciful one, and ever protect the saints.
m.chalisa.cau14: A story is told of one time: a great delusion came over your mind.
m.chalisa.cau15: Looking at your lotus seat, you reflected that there was no one else in the world.
m.chalisa.cau16: Then you took hold of the lotus stalk and vowed to see its end.
m.chalisa.cau17: Millions of years passed in this way; wandering on and on, days and nights went by.
m.chalisa.cau18: But you did not find its end; you lost hope and grew exceedingly sad.
m.chalisa.cau19: Then you thought this in your mind: this great lotus is very ancient.
m.chalisa.cau20: Why did it come into being? For this reason alone: that it bears me.
m.chalisa.cau21: In all the worlds there is no one anywhere; everything is contained within me.
m.chalisa.cau22: Resolving this, you swelled with pride and, taking yourself to be Brahman, were content.
m.chalisa.cau23: Then a deep voice came from the sky: Brahmā, hold steady and listen to my words.
m.chalisa.cau24: He who is the master of all creation is Brahman, beginningless and unseen.
m.chalisa.cau25: By his own will he created all; he made Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa.
m.chalisa.cau26: The three gods appeared for the sake of creation; the whole world will serve them.
m.chalisa.cau27: The great lotus that is your seat is under Viṣṇu's rule.
m.chalisa.cau28: It came forth from Viṣṇu's navel. I have made the truth plain to you.
m.chalisa.cau29: Go and meet Viṣṇu, regarding him as your well-wisher. Saying this, the voice from the sky fell silent.
m.chalisa.cau30: Hearing what was said, Brahmā was amazed; then the four-faced one set out.
m.chalisa.cau31: Holding the lotus stalk, he came down, and there he beheld Viṣṇu.
m.chalisa.cau32: He saw the lord of the gods lying asleep, his dark-hued body supremely incomparable.
m.chalisa.cau33: His four arms are very beautiful; a diadem-crown shines on his head.
m.chalisa.cau34: The vaijayantī garland graces his neck, putting to shame the splendour of ten million suns.
m.chalisa.cau35: Conch, discus and lovely mace, with the lotus: all his weapons are beautiful.
m.chalisa.cau36: Ramā ceaselessly presses his feet; his bed, the serpent Śeṣa, is most charming.
m.chalisa.cau37: Seeing that divine form, Brahmā bowed; the lord of Śrī, abode of happiness, was delighted.
m.chalisa.cau38: The four-faced one prayed humbly in many ways; then Lakṣmī's lord said, glad at heart:
m.chalisa.cau39: Brahmā, cast off your pride. We two are forms of Brahman, and equal.
m.chalisa.cau40: The third is Śrī Śiva. In the three worlds we are all forms of Brahman.
m.chalisa.cau41: Through you creation spreads; I shall sustain the world.
m.chalisa.cau42: Śiva brings about the destruction of all. We three have much work.
m.chalisa.cau43: Describe the blessed Brahman as without attributes; know him to be formless.
m.chalisa.cau44: We three gods are forms with shape; we shall always serve Brahman.
m.chalisa.cau45: Hearing this, Brahmā was supremely glad and sang at length the glory of the Supreme Brahman.
m.chalisa.cau46: All that is known by the name of the Veda; it is liberation itself, supremely lovely.
m.chalisa.cau47: In this way, Lord, your birth came about; then you brought the world forth.
m.chalisa.cau48: You received the lovely name Pitāmaha and created all things, inert and conscious.
m.chalisa.cau49: You took incarnation many times and spread your fair glory through the world.
m.chalisa.cau50: Gods and demons all meditate on you; all obtain from you what their hearts desire.
m.chalisa.cau51: Whoever meditates on you, man or woman, you fulfil all their hopes.
m.chalisa.cau52: The holy place of Puṣkara gives supreme happiness; there you ever dwell, king of the gods.
m.chalisa.cau53: Whoever bathes in its pool and worships, all his faults are removed.
